name: penecho
description: Think with AI beyond the chat box. A shared canvas for handwriting, equations, diagrams, and spatial reasoning.
readmeHtml:
Think on a canvas, with any AI.

Sketch by hand. PenEcho's built-in Agent — or Codex, Claude Code and any MCP
client — turns it into diagrams, documents and working widgets right beside your
notes.

What's new in 1.4 · Quick start · Connect your AI (MCP) · Docs · Discord

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Русский · Español · Português · Français · Deutsch

From a hand sketch to an interactive result in one canvas.

New in 1.4: it knows what you need

▶ Watch with sound and chapters · Download MP4
Smart Assist · PenEchoLLM · Notes & Cards · live graphs · simulations · 3D


PenEchoLLM suggests the next step
Pause after writing and PenEchoLLM ranks what you need next: Solve, Typeset, Plot graph, Make diagram, Organize as Note and more. One tap and the answer lands where you wrote, with the next step already suggested. It learns from the suggestions you choose, on your device. Free to try every day, no API key needed.
Notes & Cards keep what matters
Circle a formula, sketch or answer and keep it as a knowledge card or work note, with your original handwriting. Cards are categorized automatically and collected in the Library, where you can search, bookmark, review and bring them into any canvas.

What you can do


Sketch, then ask
Handwriting, equations, text and images on an endless canvas. PenEchoLLM suggests the next step when you pause.
Professional diagrams
Architecture, sequence and workflow diagrams with automatic layout. Export SVG or PNG.
Working widgets
Calculators, quizzes and prototypes that run on the canvas and can be favourited or shared.

Quick start

Get started
Desktop app macOS and Windows from GitHub Releases. Includes everything, updates itself.
npm Node.js 22.19+. Run npm i -g penecho then penecho and open localhost:3888.
Browser Sign in at penecho.ai for hosted models and Cloud canvases. Nothing to install. 
npm install -g penecho
penecho             # opens http://localhost:3888

Tip

On first start, choose a six-digit access code (or open access on a trusted network). Add a model in Settings → AI & connections: your own API key, a signed-in Codex / Claude Code / Kimi CLI, or PenEcho models.

Run from source 
git clone https://github.com/penecho/penecho.git
cd penecho
npm install
npm start

Connect your AI agent (MCP)

Keep talking in the agent you already use. PenEcho gives the work a place to live — your agent draws on the canvas, you mark it up, and it reads your feedback on the next turn.

  1. In PenEcho, open Settings → MCP service and turn on the current canvas.

  2. Use Auto configure for a supported client, or copy the generated setup prompt into your client (Codex, Claude Code, Kimi, Cursor...). For a global npm installation, clients that accept mcpServers JSON can also use the compatibility entry below:

    {
  "mcpServers": {
    "penecho": { "command": "penecho", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}

  3. Ask: “Show the architecture we discussed on my PenEcho canvas.”

An architecture discussion from Claude Code, annotated by hand on the canvas.

Note

Agents only see canvases you turn on. Local MCP stays on your computer; Cloud MCP is a separate signed-in connection for Cloud canvases. MCP guide →

Diagram gallery


Kubernetes cluster
Monolith → microservices
Event-driven notifications

How MCP reaches the canvas
Release: parallel tasks
Multi-region rollout

Click any diagram for the full-size version.

How it works

  • On your computer — the desktop app or CLI serves the canvas and uses your own model API or agent CLI.
  • In the cloud — penecho.ai adds hosted models, synced projects and favorites, and can reach your linked computer.
  • Your agent — connects through Local or Cloud MCP. Both are optional.

Details: architecture notes.

Choose your AI

Connection Cost Best for
PenEcho models — sign in, pick a model Account credits Getting started, no keys
Your model API — OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible Your provider Full control of model and cost
Your CLI — Codex, Claude Code or Kimi, signed in Your plan Reusing a subscription you have

Which model and effort to pick: recommended models (updated with each release).

Recommended models

These recommendations balance answer quality against the latency of PenEcho's real canvas workload, based on current hands-on testing; actual response time varies with the provider, canvas complexity, and reasoning behavior.

Model Effort Notes Recommended use
Claude Opus 4.8 / 5.0 (claude-opus-4-8 / claude-opus-5-0) medium Strong quality with a better latency balance Everyday canvas work
Claude Opus 4.8 / 5.0 (claude-opus-4-8 / claude-opus-5-0) high Higher reasoning quality, longer and more variable waits Complex handwriting, mathematics, diagrams, or layout
Fable 5 (claude-fable-5 or fable) medium Often around half the response time of gpt-5.6-sol at xhigh Fast, high-quality general use
Kimi K3 (kimi-k3) medium Very good quality; medium keeps the balance practical Recommended Kimi default
gpt-5.6-terra low to high Surprisingly strong and responsive Flexible quality and latency targets
gpt-5.6-luna xhigh Very good canvas results with strong speed Quality-first, still responsive
gpt-5.6-sol high Good enough for most requests, more responsive than xhigh Default when responsiveness matters
gpt-5.6-sol xhigh Very good but slower and more variable Difficult canvas tasks
deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp medium Good Vision-capable work through the DeepSeek API
glm-5.3-flash medium Good Fast work through the GLM Anthropic-compatible API

What's new in 1.4.0

  • Smart Assist with PenEchoLLM: context-aware actions for handwriting, text and images, ranked by PenEchoLLM, with quick answers, visual creation and follow-up questions.
  • Lasso AI: circle any part of the canvas to solve, visualize, animate or organize just the selected content.
  • Notes & Cards: turn canvas content into reusable notes and knowledge cards; browse, search and bring them into other canvases.
  • Widget refinement: refine results through written feedback and contextual actions, with clearer controls and better content fitting.
  • Canvas polish: improved pen gestures, stroke deletion, navigation and collaboration with Agent and MCP.

Watch the 1.4 tour → · Full changelog →

releases.body:
## What's New

- Improved Canvas Assist and reusable Notes & Cards.
- More reliable Canvas saves and Widget recovery.
- Added local math and 3D rendering resources.
- Fixed npm startup, upload cancellation, and packaging issues.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/penecho/penecho/compare/v1.3.5...v1.4.0

releases.name: PenEcho v1.3.5
releases.body:
PenEcho v1.3.5 brings together the key improvements from 1.3.0–1.3.5, making the Canvas a more capable workspace for you and your AI agents.

## Highlights

- **Bring your own AI agent with MCP.** Connect Codex, Claude Code, Kimi, Cursor, or other compatible clients through Local MCP or Cloud MCP. Agents can read enabled Canvases, create and edit content, work with interactive Widgets, and respond to handwritten feedback.

- **Concurrent AI collaboration.** Canvas AI, PenEcho Agent, and MCP-connected agents can work on the same Canvas simultaneously. Agent workflows also gain improved file and document handling, conversation recovery, progress reporting, and thinking controls for supported models.

- **Professional diagrams.** Create architecture, sequence, and workflow diagrams with automatic layout and connection routing. Refine them through feedback or source edits, then export SVG or PNG. Rendering runs locally in the browser.

releases.name: PenEcho v1.3.3
releases.body:
## Professional Diagrams on the Canvas

PenEcho v1.3.3 introduces architecture diagrams, sequence diagrams, and workflows—with automatic layout, interactive details, and SVG/PNG export.

Create diagrams with PenEcho Agent or an MCP-connected AI agent, then refine them through feedback or source edits. Diagram layout and rendering run locally in your browser.

### Architecture Diagrams
Visualize services, dependencies, and nested system boundaries. Automatic layout and connection routing help keep complex systems readable.

### Sequence Diagrams
Describe interactions between participants with ordered messages, replies, self-calls, and activations. Model conditional, loop, and parallel scenarios.

### Workflows
Map processes with steps, decisions, labeled branches, loops, and parallel paths, including fork and join points.

## Improvements

- **Canvas Library:** Browse larger collections with pagination, search, project filters, and sorting. Previews load as cards become visible.

releases.name: PenEcho v1.3.2 — Canvas, MCP, and desktop improvements
releases.body:
## What's Changed

- Improved Canvas reliability and document handling.
- Improved MCP connection stability, session recovery, and PenEcho Agent responses.
- Refined desktop updates and Windows first-run behavior.
- Improved metadata routing and linked-device handling.
- Refreshed application icons, installer branding, and README visuals.


**Full Changelog**: [v1.3.1...v1.3.2](https://github.com/penecho/penecho/compare/v1.3.1...v1.3.2)

releases.name: PenEcho v1.3.1
releases.body:
## PenEcho 1.3.1

PenEcho 1.3.1 turns the Canvas into a shared visual workspace for the built-in PenEcho Agent and the AI agents you already use. Move from conversation to editable diagrams, documents, interactive Widgets, and handwritten feedback — all in the same space.

### Highlights

- **Bring your own agent with MCP.** Connect Codex, Claude Code, or another MCP-compatible client through Local MCP or Cloud MCP. Agents can discover explicitly enabled Canvases, capture context, create and edit Canvas objects, work with interactive Widgets and source files, and respond to handwritten feedback.
- **More capable PenEcho Agent workflows.** Work with files and documents, create editable visual content, continue conversations reliably, and receive clearer progress and error reporting.
- **Cloud and Linked Device improvements.** Cloud Canvases load, save, and recover more reliably. Cloud features remain available without an online Linked Device, while a connected device adds access to its local files and AI connections.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A collaborative, AI-powered spatial canvas for brainstorming with handwriting and diagrams.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: PenEcho is a shared digital canvas application that integrates artificial intelligence deeply into a freeform, spatial workspace. Moving beyond traditional text-based chat interfaces, it allows users to brainstorm, draw, write equations, and create diagrams alongside an AI assistant. The platform treats spatial context—such as handwriting and visual layout—as first-class inputs for the AI, enabling a more natural and expressive ideation process. It supports multiple languages and fosters community collaboration, aiming to replicate the experience of standing at a whiteboard with an intelligent partner. It is designed to think with AI beyond the chat box.
keyFeatures: Spatial AI integration: Allows AI to understand and interact with the spatial layout of drawings, text, and diagrams on the canvas.
Handwriting recognition: Supports natural input via handwriting and sketches, processing them as actionable context.
Equation and diagram parsing: Translates visual mathematical equations and structural diagrams into structured data for the AI.
Shared canvas workflow: Provides a collaborative workspace where multiple users and AI agents can interact simultaneously.
Multi-language support: Offers comprehensive internationalization with documentation and interfaces available in over eight languages.

useCases.description: Sketch out complex system architectures and have the AI immediately generate corresponding code or structural suggestions.

useCases.title: Concept mapping

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Designers, educators, engineers, and creatives who find standard text-based LLM chat interfaces restrictive and prefer visual, spatial brainstorming tools.
